question.worked_solution:
The laws of logarithms are:

- ${log}_{n}⁡(a)+{log}_{n}⁡(b)={log}_{n}⁡(ab)$ - the product rule

- ${log}_{n}⁡(a)-{log}_{n}⁡(b)={log}_{n}⁡(\frac{a}{b})$ - the quotient rule

- ${log}_{n}⁡({c}^{m})=m{log}_{n}⁡(c)$ - the power rule

Note that ${log}_{5}⁡({x}^{2}{y}^{3})$ can be rewritten using the product and power rules as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{5}⁡({x}^{2}{y}^{3}) & ={log}_{5}⁡({x}^{2})+{log}_{5}⁡({y}^{3}) \\  & =2{log}_{5}⁡(x)+3{log}_{5}⁡(y)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since ${log}_{5}⁡(x)=3$ and ${log}_{5}⁡(y)=2$, we conclude that

$$
2{log}_{5}⁡(x)+3{log}_{5}⁡(y)=2\cdot 3+3\cdot 2=12.
$$

Hence

$$
{log}_{5}⁡({x}^{2}{y}^{3})=12.
$$
